material_blockers.summary: The provider service tier is neither fixed nor audited, so project-level Fast/Priority configuration can bypass the predeclared USD ceiling and produce a falsely low cost audit.
evidence: The packet requires unknown or changed budget fields to fail closed before client construction and requires an exact conservative price-bound cost on initial response and replay (packet lines 43–49 and 64–68).

At product commit 67f1b418ce308091b2dd7476bda32ede8df957c0, src/glupta_agi/workflow.py:41–48 omits `service_tier`; inference.py:12–20 and 63–76 assumes Standard pricing; neither ReleaseProfile nor FrozenDispatch binds the tier.
openai_adapter.py:107–120 sends that request unchanged. Lines 175–190 calculate and record cost using the Standard-only schedule, while contracts.py:46–70 has no field for the returned service tier.

The exact pinned OpenAI 2.45 SDK documents that an omitted `service_tier` behaves as `auto` and follows Project settings; explicitly setting `default` selects Standard pricing (response_create_params.py:215–230).

OpenAI permits projects to default to Fast/Priority. GPT-5.6 Sol Fast pricing is $10/M input and $60/M output, versus Standard $5/M and $30/M output. At the candidate's reserved maxima, Fast costs $2.94 while the adapter records $1.8075 and accepts it under the $1.85 ceiling. See [OpenAI Fast mode](https://openai.com/api-fast-mode/) and [GPT-5.6 Sol pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol).
material_blockers.defect_class: production-code budget-boundary defect and false closure claim
material_blockers.disposition: Keep dispatch frozen. Bind an explicit approved service tier—preferably `service_tier="default"`—through the release profile, frozen dispatch, request digest, provider audit, and response validation; add adversarial initial/replay tests. Re-freeze new exact bytes and restart the full review.

non_blocking_findings: Both supplied top-level SHA-256 values matched. All 46 manifest entries matched their exact Git blobs at the declared product, control, and Blueprint commits; declared bases and ancestry were valid.
The named R5 boundary repairs and credential-byte fingerprinting are present. I substantiated no second material blocker.
Release, provider/account evidence, deployment, dispatch, task-drain, stage, and broader-authority gates remain explicitly held and were not counted as blockers.
factual_corrections: The packet's claim of exact conservative cost enforcement on initial response and replay is true only when Standard service tier is used; these bytes do not enforce that condition.

The control amendment's statement that the code path conforms is overbroad: approved project identity does not freeze its Default Service Tier, and the request currently inherits that mutable project setting.

foundation_disposition.cost: Small, bounded production-contract and regression-test repair; no architectural rebuild indicated.
foundation_disposition.risk: Without repair, a valid project-level setting can cause charges above the reserved ceiling while durable audit records understate actual cost.
foundation_disposition.rollback: Make no remediation inside this audit. Preserve exact R5 as rejected evidence, produce a newly hashed candidate, and restart exact-candidate review; all held authorities remain frozen.

confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence. The defect follows directly from exact candidate source, the pinned SDK contract, and current official provider pricing/configuration documentation. No peer-review output, credential, or provider call was used. Read-only constraints prevented rerunning write-producing suites, but that does not affect this directly demonstrated request/budget mismatch.
